tb21_profile.skill: Recover the exact behaviour of a compiled binary - by black-box probing, decompiling or disassembly - and re-express it as independent C that reproduces its effect exactly, without calling it and without embedding its data
tb21_profile.domain: x86-64 ELF reverse engineering, C/libc, compiled-code semantics, differential testing against a reference binary
tb21_profile.task_form: reverse-engineer-a-binary then implement-from-inference, with a source-size budget (under 2KB gzipped) and a gcc -static compile-and-compare harness

TMax-15K.reason: Undocumented stripped binary is the only spec; replicate its transformation exactly so the pipeline keeps working. Same problem, different artifact.
Closed-source stripped oracle must be reimplemented so outputs agree, with performance on top; probe-deduce-reimplement end to end.
Your program must behave identically to an oracle binary, and you must build the differential harness that proves it PASS/FAIL.
Bit-exact reimplementation of a binary oracle derived purely from black-box probing - the exact standard this TB2.1 task is graded on.
Undocumented proprietary stripped binary defines a packet-inspection protocol; decode it and rebuild the logic in your own code.
Stripped legacy_cleaner with lost source: work out its text-extraction rules from behaviour and reproduce them.
A stripped token validator used as an oracle; deduce its acceptance logic from probes and reimplement it faithfully.
Use strings/objdump/ltrace or pure black-box testing to pin down a stripped binary's exact filtering rules, then reimplement them.
Reconstruct an encoder that behaves identically to a stripped binary, including where it loses precision - matching quirks, not intent.
Proprietary optimised C binary performs dimensionality reduction and quantisation; reproduce its numeric output exactly.

Recursive-Task-Synthesis.reason: Determine a crackme's expected input by analysing its code, explicitly without brute force - static reasoning about compiled logic.
Objdump-driven static analysis of a stripped crackme; the disassembly-reading half of this task, without the reimplementation half.
Recover the accepted password 'without guessing', which forces actual comprehension of the binary's comparison logic.
Three crackmes that store their secrets differently, so one trick will not solve all - forces several RE techniques.
Locate a crackme inside git history and derive the input that makes it print Congrats; retrieval plus binary analysis.
Resolve which deployment profile's crackme applies, then reverse it; environment reasoning wrapped around binary analysis.
Reverse the crackme and record each investigation step, which rewards a systematic RE method rather than a lucky guess.
Three crackme executables whose accepted inputs must be discovered and demonstrated by running them.
Use binary inspection tooling to characterise an executable and report the findings in a fixed format; analysis without rebuild.
Produce and verify a statically linked ARM64 ELF with no libc; ELF-level correctness, but nothing is being reversed.

TerminalWorld-Seeds-Clean.reason: Reverse a stripped Linux crackme with static or dynamic analysis to extract the exact expected input; graded, unlike most of this pool's RE tasks.
Three crackmes storing their passwords by different mechanisms - broad practice in reading compiled comparison logic.
Same Monologix crackme, sourced from upstream; disassembly-driven recovery of the accepted input.
Emulate a binary's key-generation logic with radare2 ESIL - reproducing an algorithm read out of machine code. Closest TW match but FREE-graded.
Emulate a binary's execution under ESIL; instruction-level understanding of compiled code. FREE verifier, so per_source only.
Symbolic execution to find the input a binary accepts; a principled way to recover a binary's behaviour. FREE verifier.
Write a quine: produce exactly the required output by construction rather than by reading it, mirroring the no-invoke/no-embed rule.
Patch a compiled binary so a check always passes; requires locating the branch in machine code. FREE verifier.
Defeat a CPU-flag-based protection in an ELF crackme; flag-level semantics of compiled code. FREE verifier.
Write and compile a C program whose stdout must match a precise format; only the gcc harness is shared.

SWE-Smith-Seeds-Clean.reason: Infer a function's real signature from observed runtime calls - inferring a specification from execution traces, which is what black-boxing a binary is.
Same trace-to-type inference machinery; the bug is in how observations become a reconstructed spec.
More of the runtime-observation-to-declaration pipeline; transferable mindset, unrelated stack.
Decode fixed-layout binary frames with bit-level field placement; the byte/bit reasoning needed to read a compiled data format.
Same binary-signal codec library; encode/decode round-trip fidelity is the local analogue of output equality.
Parsing an opaque document format's internal objects; format archaeology, but the fix is an ordinary Python bug.
CLI behaviour must match a documented contract exactly, including exit behaviour; behavioural-parity mindset only.
Inferring structure from raw bytes without metadata; weak but genuine overlap with reading an unknown binary.
Deterministic table-driven transformation whose output must match a reference exactly; only the exactness transfers.
Quota filler: Python parser fidelity, no compiled artifact anywhere in sight.

SWE-Rebench-Tasks-Clean.reason: An interpreter for 010-editor binary templates: declaring and walking the layout of an unknown binary is the core RE workflow.
Same binary-template engine, different interpreter fault; still the 'describe an unknown file's structure' capability.
Third pfp issue; the library exists precisely to reverse-engineer binary formats, which is the nearest Rebench gets.
Semantics of a compiled circuit representation must be preserved across a transformation; compile-and-preserve-meaning reasoning.
Traced/compiled execution must agree with the eager reference; an equivalence-between-two-implementations bug.
Parsing and round-tripping a structured binary/text music format; format fidelity, no compiled code.
Command-line behavioural parity across versions; matching another implementation's observable behaviour, at a high level.
Quota filler: packaging metadata handling shares nothing with binary reversal.
Quota filler: task-queue regression, no artifact to reverse.
Quota filler: log rotation timing bug, unrelated.

Terminal-Lego-15k.reason: Copy a function's machine code out of .text into heap memory and execute it; requires understanding how compiled code is laid out and protected.
Hide secrets in a binary so they resist trivial extraction - the defender's side of exactly this task. FREE-graded, so per_source only.
Disassemble an executable and read its assembly; the primary tool of this task, taught at tutorial depth. FREE verifier.
Edit RPATH inside an already-compiled ELF; direct manipulation of binary structure rather than of source.
Statically embed resources into an ELF and read them back at runtime; how data lives inside a compiled artifact.
Analyse a core dump in GDB for a program taking arguments; extracting state from a compiled process.
Determine only the direct shared-object dependencies of an ELF; reading ELF metadata rather than behaviour.
Get zlib to decompress gzip correctly in C - an exact-format implementation task, though the algorithm is not reversed.
Detect gzip by its magic bytes in C; the smallest possible slice of reading a binary file's structure.
C program that resolves the path of its own executable; process/ELF introspection, well verified but shallow here.

Figure out exactly what /app/oracle does and reimplement it in C matching stdout, stderr and exit behaviour for all inputs.
my_vm.c must produce output identical to /app/vm for any bytecode file, compiled gcc -static -O2; an entire instruction set must be inferred.
Reconstruct a custom bytecode VM from four sample programs, self-contained, explicitly forbidden from invoking the reference.
/app/compress's source is gone; reimplement its custom codec in C so the formats interoperate, under an 8K gzip budget, without invoking it.
Infer an undocumented LZSS container's exact layout from sample files and implement it in C under 1800 bytes - inference plus size budget.
Your compressor's output must be byte-for-byte what the original produces for ANY input; matching an unseen implementation exactly.
From-scratch DEFLATE in C under a 3KB gzip cap, no libraries and no reading the answer - the same anti-embedding device.
Emulate a syscall interface so the program produces the same output as running it natively; behavioural equivalence at the ABI level.
Decoder in C compiled gcc -static with the source capped at 300 gzipped bytes; extreme version of the algorithmic-not-embedded constraint.

final_top10.reason: Word-for-word this task: /app/mystery compiled binary, write independent /app/hash.c, gcc -static compile-and-diff, must not invoke mystery, under 1500 bytes gzipped. Tests diff against the live binary over empty/simple/long/all-256-byte/position-sensitive inputs.
An oracle binary must be understood exactly and reimplemented in C matching stdout, stderr and exit behaviour for all inputs - the TB2.1 task with a different payload.
Reconstruct a whole VM from a reference binary so stdout matches for any bytecode, compiled gcc -static; same harness, same independence rule.
Infer a custom instruction set from four sample programs and rebuild the VM in self-contained C that must not invoke the original.
Source-less compression binary must be reimplemented in C compatible with its format, under a gzip source budget, without calling it.
An undocumented stripped binary is the only specification; replicate its transformation exactly.
Behave identically to an oracle binary and build the differential harness that proves it - teaches the verification loop as well as the RE.
Deduce an undocumented compressed format from samples alone and implement it in C under 1800 bytes; inference plus the size budget.
Closed-source stripped oracle reimplemented so its outputs agree; adds a performance requirement on top of exact behavioural match.
Decode an undocumented proprietary stripped binary's protocol and rebuild its decision logic in C; strongly pinned verifier.

notes: Very well served by two pools. CalibForge has a purpose-built family of 'here is a compiled binary, write independent C that reproduces it, under a gzip source budget, do not invoke it' tasks that are plainly siblings of this TB2.1 seed; TMax-15K has a large, well-verified stripped-binary-reimplementation family. The honest top 10 is entirely CalibForge and TMax. The single most important item for the merge step is software-engineering_20260607_104421_016: it is the closest task in the pool and its FREE grade is a false negative (its tests are a differential comparison against the reference binary plus a source grep forbidding ./mystery). I obeyed the hard rule and left it out of final_top10, but if the grade is corrected it belongs at rank 1. TerminalWorld and Recursive-Task-Synthesis both have real reverse-engineering content, but it is almost entirely the same handful of crackme binaries (Crackme-Monologix, Crackit-GCI, crackme0x00) repeated dozens of times, it stops at 'find the password' rather than 'reimplement the program', and in TerminalWorld most of it is FREE-graded (tw_42850, tw_134335, tw_229615, tw_165683, tw_21329). Terminal-Lego-15k could not field 10 defensible candidates: it has no reverse-engineering task at all, only tutorials about objdump, gdb and ELF metadata, so its ranks 3-10 are honest 2s. SWE-Rebench is weakest; only the d0c-s4vage/pfp binary-template issues are real.
